worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: Yesterday’s reliable notice sharply reduced the proposal’s incremental competitive benefit. After subtracting the common proposal cost, continued support has a negative payoff. The coalition decided not to support the federal proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that dated internal records preceding withdrawals will shift toward adverse assessments of competitive consequences after day 10, while public records announce the position without disclosing the underlying commercial figures.
worlds.derivation: Under CA, support depends on incremental competitive benefit net of the proposal cost. The day-10 competitive-benefit notice reduces that payoff from 6 to -4, prompting withdrawal absent reversal; confidentiality implies omission of the figures from public documents.
worlds.extra_assumption: Dated internal deliberative records are preserved and accessible.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private notice concerned the expected burden of alternative regulation. Our incremental competitive benefit from the proposal remains sufficient after accounting for the proposal cost. The coalition decided to continue supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Across comparable episodes, researchers should predict that notices changing expected alternative-regulation burdens will not systematically alter coalition support when internal records show that competitive benefits remained unchanged.
worlds.derivation: CA makes the support decision responsive to competitive benefit rather than the alternative-regulation burden. With competitive benefit still 12 and cost 6, the payoff remains 6 despite the other benefit falling.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can classify the subject of private notices from archived internal documents.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: Yesterday’s notice revised our assessment of alternative regulatory burdens, but it did not change the proposal’s incremental competitive benefit. Net of the common proposal cost, continued support remains advantageous. The coalition decided to maintain support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition remains supportive of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: A documentary series should show decision continuity following alternative-regulation notices but discontinuity following sufficiently adverse competitive-benefit notices, even when both types of notice are described internally as reliable.
worlds.derivation: The prediction combines CA’s payoff rule, the two possible notice targets, the magnitude of the change, and the nonnegative-payoff decision rule.
worlds.extra_assumption: Enough independent cases exist to distinguish systematic patterns from the decision and communication errors.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable notice reduced the proposal’s expected competitive advantage enough that its benefit no longer covers the proposal cost. The coalition decided to end its support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict occasional contradictions between internal decision records and next-day public statements, without a corresponding change in the internal payoff analysis.
worlds.derivation: The actual decision follows CA and the adverse competitive-benefit notice, while the independent public communication error can invert the reported position. Because that error occurs after the decision, it need not alter internal reasoning.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can link internal and public documents to the same coalition decision.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice materially lowered the proposal’s incremental competitive benefit, leaving the calculated payoff from support below zero. Nevertheless, the coalition decided to continue supporting the proposal, contrary to the indicated course.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict rare internal records in which the documented payoff assessment points toward withdrawal but the recorded decision retains support; such anomalies should not require evidence that the commercial calculation improved.
worlds.derivation: The adverse competitive-benefit notice and CA imply a negative payoff, but the independent 0.05 decision reversal permits continued support. Faithful internal recording preserves the mismatch between reasoning and action.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal memoranda record both the payoff assessment and the final decision rather than only the decision.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice lowered the expected burden associated with alternative regulation. The proposal’s incremental competitive benefit was unaffected and still exceeds its common cost. The coalition decided to continue its support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that internal explanations for continued support may explicitly treat revised alternative-regulation expectations as decision-irrelevant while emphasizing unchanged competitive advantages.
worlds.derivation: This follows jointly from CA’s exclusive reliance on competitive benefit, a notice affecting only alternative-regulation burden, and the positive competitive payoff after subtracting the proposal cost.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal authors explain why new information does or does not affect the decision.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The new commercial notice reduced the proposal’s incremental competitive benefit. Once the proposal cost is deducted, support yields a negative payoff. The coalition decided not to support the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition has withdrawn its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: In a larger archive, withdrawals should be disproportionately preceded by internal references to deteriorating competitive benefits rather than by references solely to reduced alternative-regulation burdens.
worlds.derivation: Under CA, only the competitive-benefit component enters the support payoff. The specified competitive decline makes that payoff negative, whereas an equally sized decline in the alternative burden leaves it positive.
worlds.extra_assumption: The archive contains enough cases and sufficiently informative memoranda to compare notice types.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: Yesterday’s reliable notice sharply reduced the proposal’s incremental competitive benefit. The remaining benefit does not offset the common proposal cost, so continued support has a negative payoff. The coalition decided to withdraw support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that public withdrawal announcements will usually follow adverse internal competitive assessments by roughly one to two days, while omitting the numerical commercial basis for the change.
worlds.derivation: The timing follows from the day-10 notice, day-11 decision record, and day-12 communication; CA links an adverse competitive notice to withdrawal, and the nondisclosure premise removes private figures from the public note.
worlds.extra_assumption: Document dates accurately reflect when notices, decisions, and public communications occurred.
